paper_title: A Telescope Search for Decaying Relic Axions
notes: VLT/VIMOS-IFU search for optical two-photon decay line of thermal relic eV-mass axions in clusters A2667 & A2390, window 4.5-7.7 eV. Paper bounds the model-dependent two-photon coupling xi=(4/3)(E/N-1.92) (Eq.3), NOT g_agamma directly. Reported headline 95% CL direct upper limits on xi are Table I (derived directly from sky-subtracted spectra with the fiducial strong-lensing mass map; this is the excluded-region boundary shown in the Fig.8 comparison/money plot, file fepd.eps): (m_a[eV],xi)=(4.5,7.17e-3),(5,9.00e-3),(6,5.72e-3),(6.5,4.60e-3),(7,3.41e-3),(7.5,2.95e-3),(7.65,2.47e-3). Converted each to the canonical g_agamma via the paper's own lifetime relation tau=6.8e24 xi^-2 m_a,eV^-5 s (Eq.3) combined with Gamma_{a->gg}=g_agamma^2 m_a^3/(64pi): g_agamma=sqrt(64pi/(tau_nat m_a^3)), giving g_agamma[GeV^-1]=1.395e-10*xi*m_a,eV (agrees within ~10% with g_agamma=(alpha/2pi)(1/f_a)(3/4)xi using m_a=5.7ueV*1e12GeV/f_a). Values non-monotonic (peak at m=5) because sky-line contamination near 5.4-5.9 eV degrades the limit. Alternative: the most-conservative-over-density-profile curve (Fig.7 thick solid, bothd.eps; extracted xi~0.006-0.024) is ~1.4-2.4x weaker than Table I at low mass and converges at high mass; abstract quotes xi<=0.003-0.017 spanning best-direct and worst-conservative. dm_density null: limit assumes the thermal-freezeout relic abundance Omega_a h^2=m_a,eV/130 (Eq.1) and the lensing-measured cluster mass density, not an assumed local halo density.
